title: Mali and Mansa Musa
text: In the fourteenth century, the Mali Empire controlled important routes carrying gold and salt across West Africa. Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca displayed enormous wealth and connected Mali to a wider scholarly world. Timbuktu became known for trade and learning, though its history reaches beyond any single ruler.
context: An introduction to medieval Mali and trans-Saharan exchange.
vocabulary: pilgrimage: a journey to a sacred place

title: Ideas in Song China
text: During China's Song dynasty, printers produced books with carved blocks and movable type. Engineers improved clocks, ships, canals, and iron production. Merchants used paper money on a large scale. These developments did not appear all at once, but together they reveal a complex and inventive society.
context: A broad overview of selected Song-era innovations.
vocabulary: dynasty: a succession of rulers from one family
movable type: reusable characters for printing

title: Roads Across the Andes
text: The Inca governed a vast Andean realm without wheeled transport or a conventional written script. Roads, bridges, runners, storehouses, and knotted records called quipu helped connect high mountains and valleys. Their achievement depended on organized labor, while imperial rule also placed heavy demands on conquered communities.
context: An introduction to Inca administration before Spanish conquest.
vocabulary: Andean: relating to the Andes Mountains
quipu: knotted cords used for records

title: Reading an Ocean
text: Polynesian navigators crossed immense stretches of the Pacific using stars, winds, currents, clouds, birds, and patterns of ocean swell. Their knowledge was learned through careful teaching and experience. Navigation joined observation with memory, proving that a map can exist in trained understanding as well as on paper.
context: A respectful overview of traditional Pacific wayfinding.
vocabulary: wayfinding: determining and following a route

title: The Translation Movement
text: Scholars working in Abbasid Baghdad translated and studied writings from Greek, Persian, Indian, and other traditions. They did more than preserve old books: they criticized, extended, and reorganized knowledge in mathematics, medicine, astronomy, and philosophy. Later scholars in many regions built on this work.
context: An overview of scholarship centered in Baghdad from the eighth to tenth centuries.
vocabulary: Abbasid: relating to a major Islamic caliphate

title: Haiti Wins Independence
text: Enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue began a revolution in 1791. After years of conflict, Haiti declared independence in 1804 and abolished slavery. The revolution challenged empires that proclaimed liberty while profiting from bondage. Its leaders and factions had complex aims and fierce disagreements.
context: A non-graphic summary of the Haitian Revolution.
vocabulary: colony: territory controlled by another country
